cards.note: Clusters of Khasi pines growing on hills are very typical of far northeastern Vietnam, specifically the provinces of Lạng Sơn and Quảng Ninh.
In central regions like Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi, and Bình Định, acacia plantations can sometimes be found Quảng Nam Province Quảng Ngãi Province Bình Định Province
Thin bamboo poles can be found in rural areas of the northwestern mountains.
The area along ĐT651 is a resort zone with white sandy beaches along the road.
Poles in the northern parts of the country will often have black pole stickers, similar to those found in Malaysia but often with a more simple design.
EVN CPC pole found in central Vietnam : "Mountain + △" shape
Coffee production is concentrated in provinces around Tây Nguyên

Dragonfruit farms are mostly found in two small areas in the south:

around the city of Phan Thiết in Bình Thuận province

a small area on the border between Long An and Tiền Giang, northeast of Mỹ Tho .

Dragonfruit resembles the end of an upturned wet mop.

cards.a: Hội An - Town of Hoi An
cards.note: The town of Hội An is an ancient town located southeast of Da Nang. The architecture is distinct, using lots of yellow buildings, and there is a river running through the town. They also like to spam lamps everywhere.

cards.a: Khanh Hoa - Khanh Hoa Meter box
cards.note: Meter Box Designs with trap door style windows plus ventilation slits on the sides are very common in the province of Khanh Hoa. It can be found everywhere in the province from rural villages to coastal areas. Note that other regular Meter box designs can be found throughout the whole country.

cards.a: max south road - Max south road
cards.note: This road max south in Vietnam is recognizable. You can usually see canals, and you are surrounded by rows of trees. The road is at a constant northwest angle.
Houses in the Mekong Delta also have a boxy, concrete look, but are usually much less tall: they almost always consist of just a single, ground-level storey.

If you see a bit flat open area with lots of canals, it’s gonna be either the very south bit around the Mekong Delta, the northern delta, or one of several other bits along the coast. The Mekong delta is very recognizable but idk if I can exactly explain why, but I often do confuse the northern delta with the smaller bits. Looking at the buildings will help, and also the alignment of the canals and comparing it with the map. If you see mountains in the distance, it’s not the Mekong delta, and if they’re northern mountains it’ll be the northern delta.
Móng Cái is a city active in trade with China, where Mandarin and Cantonese are also spoken. Chinese-language signage and duty-free shops can be found
Wooden fences made out of sticks, or even bamboo, in a grid-like pattern, similar to fences commonly found in northeastern India, are found in the northern parts of Vietnam.

If you see a bit flat open area with lots of canals, it’s gonna be either the very south bit around the Mekong Delta, the northern delta, or one of several other bits along the coast. The Mekong delta is very recognizable but idk if I can exactly explain why, but I often do confuse the northern delta with the smaller bits. Looking at the buildings will help, and also the alignment of the canals and comparing it with the map. If you see mountains in the distance, it’s not the Mekong delta, and if they’re northern mountains it’ll be the northern delta.
Houses in the north tend to have spikes in the corners.
The north has very distinct mountains. Look at some images and you’ll never confuse them with the southern mountains.
Poles with holes going all the way to the top is a strong indicator of the northern region.
Pepper plantations exists in the Đắk Nông Province and the Đắk Lắk Province
Phú Quốc Island, an offshore island near Cambodia, is also covered. The roads are often either unpaved with red soil or four-lane roads with a large median strip
Rubber plantations can be found near Tay Ninh
The area around Pleiku is fairly flat with red soil, similar to the area of Cambodia that it borders. The more southern areas bordering Cambodia are very dry but not as red.

Houses in the Red River Delta (the flat, densely populated area around Hanoi) tend to have a boxy look, typically tall with multiple storeys. These houses often feature gaudy details that borrow heavily from antique Greco-Roman architecture: pillars, pediments, classical-looking balconies, etc.

Note that similar houses are sometimes found in the direct vicinity of Ho Chi Minh City.
The coastal region northeast of Phan Thiết city is noticeably dry and sandy, compared to the typical Vietnamese landscape. Some parts of this region are very rocky as well.

Houses in the south on the other hand usually have metal roofs that are blue or white, and are often flat whereas northern ones are usually slanted. They also often have these metal awning things that come out of the front of the house and curve down. These are also common in Thailand but in Vietnam I’ve only ever seen them in the south, like in the general area of Ho Chi Min city and below.
Tea plantations are found in the northern and central mountainous regions Phu Tho Province Cao Bằng Province Lâm Đồng Province — high production, but possibly limited Street View coverage
The northern rice fields around Thanh Hóa and Nghệ An usually have a distinct vibe, consisting of a flat, agricultural landscape with hills commonly visible in the distance.

Traditional wooden houses are common in the northwest. They commonly have one or several of the following features:

Stilts holding up the house,

corrugated metal roofs,

triangular openings on the side of the roofs.
The pocket near vinh has dry and red soil
